title: The rate eased for a second week; Marseilles is still the binding lock
standfirst: The system average is down about 2% to $13.46 a ton, corn export demand holds firm, and the forward read is withheld as too stale to publish.
meta_description: Weekly nowcast of U.S. inland barge rate pressure, lock constraints, and grain export demand.
ledger_finding: Rate pressure eased to $13.46 a ton, about 2% off the prior week, with Marseilles still the binding lock.
ledger_evidence: Rate nowcast, USDA FAS · modeled + observed

paragraphs: The system-average modeled rate slipped to $13.46 a ton in the rate-week ending June 23, 2026, from $13.76 the week before — about 2% lower — and the average pressure index fell from 40.2 to 36.1. That is an elevated market cooling at the margin, not a break.

The Illinois system stays the tightest corridor and Marseilles stays the binding lock, at 13.2 hours average wait on June 26. The forward read is withheld this week: the forward leg's newest snapshot was 25 days old at publication, past the freshness line. Read the note.

sections.html:
Rate pressure is easing at the margin. The system-average modeled rate slipped to $13.46/ton (from $13.76, about 2% below the prior week) and the average pressure index fell 40.2 → 36.1 — an elevated-but-cooling market, not a break.

The Illinois system stays the tightest corridor, Marseilles is the binding chokepoint, and corn is the demand engine. The forward read is withheld this week: the forward leg's newest snapshot is 25 days old, past the freshness line.

sections.html:
Marseilles is the lock that binds

Lock friction is concentrated at Marseilles on the Illinois River. The most recent reading is June 26, 2026: 14 tows and a 13.2 hour average wait — the queue building even as the per-tow wait came down from 18.4 hours on June 21. Twenty of the twenty reviewed lock-days in the window are flagged as constraints.

The 10-day forecast points the low-water watch at the three upper-basin gauges with the lowest forward flows: USGS gauge 05331000 at 10.4 thousand cubic feet per second and a 3.5 foot stage, 05420500 at 52.2 and 9.3 feet, and 06893000 at 62.7 and 13.7 feet.
